newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian party calls for phone standard review.
newsitem.headline: Australian party calls for phone standard review.

text.p: The Australian Democrats, a minority party, on Friday called for a review of mobile phone safety following evidence that the phones might cause cancer, but the government said the Democrats were being alarmist.

Telecommunications spokeswoman Lyn Allison said that studies had indicated exposure to microwave emissions from mobile phones increased the likelihood of cancer and Australia needed to ask whether the standard was sufficient.
A spokesman for Communications Minister Richard Alston said that emissions were constantly being monitored and there was no substantial evidence to say that there was a problem.
"All the Democrats are doing is scaring people and they have no basis to do it as Australia has one of the toughest standards in the world," the spokesman told Reuters.
"We've instigated a A$4.5 million programme for education and research into the issue of electromagnetic energy, which deals with radiation emissions," he said.

A Royal Adelaide Hospital study, released on Wednesday, showed that cancer rates almost doubled in mice after prolonged exposure to radiofrequency (RF) electromagnetic fields of the type used in mobile phones.
Allison said: "Significantly, this study recorded the damage at power levels similar to those 'deemed' safe by the Australian standard."
But the Australian government said that, while the research was a useful contribution, the cancer risk on humans of mobile phones was minimal.
"The point about that study was that the emissions that they were using were well above normal emission standards," Alston's spokesman said.
Dr Michael Repacholi, chief scientist at the Royal Adelaide Hospital, said further research was needed to determine any conclusive effects on humans.
GSM is an international mobile phone transmission standard.
